Surah Fatir [Meccan, and its verses are 45 or 46; it was revealed after Al-Furqan]

﴿All praise is due to Allah﴾: He praised Himself with this, as He made clear at the beginning of Surah Saba. ﴿Originator of the heavens and the earth﴾: their Creator, without a prior pattern. ﴿Who made the angels messengers﴾ to the prophets, ﴿having wings, two or three or four﴾ and ﴿He adds to creation what He wills﴾ among the angels and others.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 35, verse 2:

﴿Whatever mercy Allah opens to the people, none can withhold; and whatever He withholds, none can release after Him.﴾ [Mercy] such as provision and rain. ﴿So none can withhold it﴾, and whatever He withholds [of that], ﴿none can release it after Him﴾, i.e., after His withholding it. ﴿And He is the Mighty﴾, the Dominant over His affair, ﴿the Wise﴾ in His action.

O people (i.e., the people of Makkah), remember the favour of God upon you by settling you in the Sacred Precinct (al-Haram) and by warding off raids from you. ﴿Is there any creator other than God﴾ — min is extra (za'ida), and khaliq is the subject (mubtada'). ﴿Other than God﴾ is in the nominative and genitive: it is an epithet (na't) of khaliq both in its wording and its grammatical position, and the predicate (khabar) of the subject is ﴿who provides for you from the heaven﴾, i.e., rain, ﴿and the earth﴾, i.e., plants. The interrogative is for affirmation (taqrir), meaning: there is no creator or provider other than Him. ﴿There is no god but Him; so how are you turned away﴾, i.e., from where are you diverted from His monotheism, while you acknowledge that He is the Creator and Provider?

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 35, verse 4:

﴿And if they deny you﴾, O Muhammad, regarding your coming with tawhid (the affirmation of God's oneness), the resurrection, the reckoning and the punishment, ﴿then messengers before you were denied﴾ regarding that. So be patient as they were patient. ﴿And to Allah all matters are returned﴾ in the Hereafter, so He will requite the deniers and grant victory to the messengers.

﴿O mankind, indeed the promise of Allah﴾ of the Resurrection and other matters ﴿is true. So let not the worldly life deceive you﴾ from belief in that ﴿and let not the Deceiver deceive you concerning Allah﴾ regarding His forbearance and His respite ﴿the Deceiver﴾ is Satan.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 35, verse 6:

﴿Indeed, Satan is an enemy to you, so take him as an enemy﴾ by obeying Allah, and do not obey him. ﴿He only invites his party﴾ his followers in disbelief, ﴿so that they may be among the companions of the Blaze﴾ the intense Fire.

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 35, verse 7:

﴿Those who disbelieve, for them is a severe punishment; and those who believe and do righteous deeds, for them is forgiveness and a great reward.﴾ This is an explanation of what is for those who agree with Satan and what is for those who oppose him.

It was revealed concerning Abu Jahl and others: ﴿Is one whose evil deed has been made attractive to him, by embellishment (al-tamwih), so that he sees it as good?﴾ Here the subject (mubtada') is "one whose evil deed," and its predicate (khabar) is omitted. The omitted predicate is indicated by what follows: ﴿like one whom Allah has guided?﴾ ﴿Indeed, Allah leads astray whom He wills and guides whom He wills, so do not let yourself waste away ﴾ over them ﴿in regret﴾ over the ones who have embellished it for them, through your grief that they do not believe. ﴿Indeed, Allah is Knowing of what they do﴾, and so He will recompense them for it.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 35, verse 9:

﴿And Allah is the One who sends the winds﴾, and in another reading: "the wind" (al-rih), ﴿so they stir up clouds﴾. The present tense (tuthir, "stir up") is used to narrate a past situation as if it were happening now (hikayat al-hal al-madiyya), meaning: it drives them along. ﴿Then We drive it﴾: there is a shift (iltifat) here from the third person (ghaybah) to the first person plural. ﴿To a dead land﴾ (baladin mayyit), read with shaddah and without shaddah (both readings are acceptable), in which there is no vegetation. ﴿So We revive the earth thereby﴾ (min al-balad, meaning the land) ﴿after its death﴾, i.e., its dryness; that is, We cause crops and pasture to grow by it. ﴿Thus will be the resurrection﴾, i.e., the raising from the dead (al-ba'th) and the bringing to life (al-ihya').

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 35, verse 10:

﴿Whoever desires might, then to Allah belongs all might.﴾ That is, in this world and the Hereafter. So you will not attain it from Him except through obedience to Him; so let him obey Him. ﴿To Him ascends the good word.﴾ He knows it, and it is "There is no god but Allah" and the like. ﴿And righteous deed raises it.﴾ He accepts it. ﴿As for those who plot evil deeds﴾ the plots ﴿against the Prophet﴾ in the Dar al-Nadwa (the assembly house of the Quraysh), such as restricting him, killing him, or expelling him, as was mentioned in Surat al-Anfal. ﴿For them is a severe punishment, and the plotting of those—it will perish.﴾ It will be destroyed.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 35, verse 11:

﴿And Allah created you from dust﴾ by the creation of your father Adam from it, ﴿then from a drop of semen﴾ i.e., from me, by the creation of his offspring from it, ﴿then He made you pairs﴾ males and females. ﴿And no female conceives or gives birth except with His knowledge﴾ a circumstantial clause, i.e., known to Him. ﴿And none is granted a lengthened life, nor is anything reduced from his lifespan﴾ i.e., nothing is added to the life of one who is granted a long life, ﴿nor is anything reduced from his lifespan﴾ i.e., of that person who is granted life, or of another person, ﴿except that it is in a Record﴾ which is the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawh al-Mahfuz). ﴿Indeed, that is easy for Allah﴾ effortless.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 35, verse 12:

﴿And not alike are the two seas: this one sweet, palatable [ʿadhb Furāt], its drink pleasant (sāʾigh sharābuh)﴾ extremely sweet (shadīd al-ʿudhūba), ﴿and this one salty, bitter [ujāj]﴾ extremely salty (shadīd al-milūḥa). ﴿And from each of them﴾ from both of them ﴿you eat fresh flesh﴾ which is fish, ﴿and you extract﴾ from the salt water; it is also said, from both of them, ﴿an ornament which you wear﴾ which is pearls and coral. ﴿And you see﴾ you observe ﴿the ships﴾ the boats ﴿therein﴾ in each of them ﴿plowing﴾ cutting through the water, i.e., splitting it with their passage, going forward and backward with one wind, ﴿that you may seek﴾ you may seek ﴿of His bounty﴾ exalted is He, through trade, ﴿and that you may give thanks﴾ to God for that.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 35, verse 13:

﴿He causes the night to enter into the day﴾ (i.e., God makes it enter), so that it increases; ﴿and He causes the day to enter into the night﴾ (i.e., He makes it enter), so that it increases; ﴿and He has subjected the sun and the moon, each of them running﴾ in its orbit ﴿for a term appointed﴾, which is the Day of Resurrection. ﴿That is God, your Lord; to Him belongs the dominion. And those you invoke﴾ (i.e., worship) ﴿besides Him﴾ (i.e., other than Him, and they are the idols) ﴿do not possess even a qitmir﴾ (the thin membrane on a date-stone), because of its worthlessness.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 35, verse 14:

﴿If you call upon them, they will not hear your call; and even if they heard, they would not respond to you﴾ supposing it, ﴿and on the Day of Resurrection they will disavow your association (of them with Allah)﴾ i.e., your associating them with Allah; that is, they will disown you and your worship of them, ﴿and none can inform you﴾ about the conditions of the two abodes ﴿like the One who is All-Aware﴾, who is Allah, exalted is He.
O mankind, you are the poor (in need) toward Allah in every respect, and Allah is the Free of need (independent) of His creation, the Praiseworthy in His acts toward them.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 35, verse 16:

﴿If He wills, He will remove you and bring a new creation﴾ instead of you.
﴿And that is not difficult for Allah at all﴾ (شَدِيد: difficult, hard)

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 35, verse 18:

﴿And no bearer of burdens shall bear the burden of another﴾, i.e., no sinful soul shall carry the sin of another soul. ﴿And if one heavily laden calls [another] to its load﴾, i.e., a soul weighed down with sin calls someone to carry some of its burden, ﴿none of it will be carried, even if he were a close relative﴾, i.e., the one called is a kinsman, such as a father or a son. The non-bearing in both cases is a ruling from Allah. ﴿You only warn those who fear their Lord unseen﴾, i.e., who fear Him, though they have not seen Him, because they are the ones who benefit from the warning. ﴿And establish prayer﴾, i.e., keep it up. ﴿And whoever purifies himself﴾, i.e., purifies himself from polytheism and other things, ﴿purifies himself only for his own soul﴾, so his good is for himself alone. ﴿And to Allah is the final destination﴾, i.e., the return, whereupon He will recompense for deeds in the Hereafter.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 35, verse 19:

﴿And the blind and the seeing are not alike﴾ — the disbeliever and the believer.
﴿Nor are the darknesses﴾ (i.e., disbelief) ﴿nor the light﴾ (i.e., faith).

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on Surah 35, verse 21:

﴿Nor is the shade [equal to] the heat-wind.﴾ [The shade is] Paradise and [the heat-wind is] the Fire.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 35, verse 22:

﴿And the living and the dead are not alike.﴾ [That is:] the believers [and] the disbelievers. [The particle] "lā" (not) in "wa-lā" (nor) [in the verse] is extra (ziyāda), [serving as] emphasis in the three [instances] (fī al-thalātha, i.e., the three negations in the context: "lā," "lā," and "lā"), ﴿Indeed, Allah causes to hear whomever He wills﴾ [i.e., whomever He wills to guide], so He responds to him with faith. ﴿But you cannot make those in the graves hear﴾ [i.e., the disbelievers]; He has likened them to the dead, and they do not respond.

﴿إنْ﴾ ما ﴿أنْتَ إلّا نَذِير﴾ مُنْذِر لَهُمْ

(﴿In﴾ ما, here "ma" as a negation, ﴿you are but a warner﴾) munthir (warner) to them.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 35, verse 24:

﴿Indeed, We have sent you with the truth﴾ with the guidance, ﴿as a bearer of good tidings﴾ to whoever responds to it, ﴿and a warner﴾ to whoever does not respond to it. ﴿And there is not a nation﴾ — ﴿in﴾ (إنْ) here is [the negation] "mā" — ﴿but has passed on﴾ [has] gone before, ﴿within it a warner﴾ a prophet who warns it.

﴿And if they deny you﴾, i.e., the people of Makkah, ﴿then those before them also denied. Their messengers came to them with the clear proofs﴾, meaning the miracles, ﴿and with the scriptures﴾, such as the Suhuf (scrolls) of Ibrahim, ﴿and with the illuminating Book﴾, which is the Tawrat (Torah) and the Injil (Gospel). ﴿So be patient, as they were patient.﴾

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 35, verse 26:

﴿Then I seized those who disbelieved﴾ for their denial, ﴿so how was My rejection﴾ (nakir), i.e. My disapproval of them through punishment and destruction. That is, it was fitting and well-placed.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 35, verse 27:

﴿Have you not seen﴾ you know (taʿlam) ﴿that Allah sends down water from the sky, and We bring forth thereby fruits of varying colors﴾ There is a shift (iltifat) here from the third person (ghaybah) ﴿such as green, red, yellow, and other colors﴾ ﴿And among the mountains are streaks﴾ plural of judda, a path or streak in the mountain and elsewhere ﴿white and red﴾ and yellow ﴿of varying shades﴾ in intensity and lightness ﴿and jet-black﴾ coordinated with judad, meaning rocks that are intensely black. It is often said: aswad ghirbib (intensely black), and less commonly: ghirbib aswad.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 35, verse 28:

﴿And among mankind, and the moving creatures, and the cattle, are those of various colors, likewise.﴾ Like the difference in fruits and mountains. ﴿Only those among His servants who have knowledge fear Allah.﴾ Unlike the ignorant, such as the disbelievers of Mecca. ﴿Indeed, Allah is Almighty⌉ in His dominion, ﴿Forgiving⌉ of the sins of His believing servants.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 35, verse 29:

﴿Indeed, those who recite﴾ the Book of Allah, i.e., read it, ﴿and establish the prayer﴾, i.e., maintain it, ﴿and spend from what We have provided them, secretly and openly﴾ in zakat and other than it, ﴿hoping for a commerce that will never perish﴾, i.e., will never be ruined.
﴿That He may pay them their rewards﴾, the reward of their deeds mentioned above, ﴿and increase them of His bounty. Indeed, He is All-Forgiving﴾ of their sins, ﴿All-Appreciative﴾ of their obedience.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 35, verse 31:

﴿And that which We have revealed to you of the Book﴾ the Qur'an ﴿is the truth, confirming what is before it﴾ of the earlier Books that preceded it ﴿Indeed, Allah is, concerning His servants, All-Aware, All-Seeing﴾ knowing the inward and the outward.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 35, verse 32:

﴿Then We caused to inherit﴾ We gave ﴿the Book﴾ the Qur'an ﴿to those whom We have chosen from Our servants﴾ and they are your ummah. ﴿So among them is one who wrongs himself﴾ by falling short in acting upon it. ﴿And among them is one who is moderate﴾ who acts upon it most of the time. ﴿And among them is one who is foremost in good deeds﴾ who combines knowledge with teaching and guiding to action. ﴿By permission of Allah﴾ by His will. ﴿That﴾ i.e., their being made to inherit the Book.

**[Tafsir al-Jalalayn by al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti, on Surah 35, verse 33]**

﴿Gardens of Eden﴾, i.e., a place of lasting residence. ﴿They will enter them﴾: the three groups enter them. The verb is read in both the active and the passive voice (بِالبِنَاءِ لِلْفَاعِلِ وَلِلْمَفْعُولِ, *bi'l-binā' lil-fā'il wa lil-maf'ūl*). ﴿Gardens﴾ (جَنَّات, *jannāt*) is the subject (al-mubtada', "the topic"), and ﴿they will enter them﴾ is its predicate (khabar). ﴿They will be adorned﴾ (يُحَلَّوْنَ, *yuḥallawna*) is a second predicate (khabar thānin). ﴿In them, of﴾ (فِيهَا مِنْ), where "some" (بَعْض, *ba'ḍ*) is implied: ﴿some bracelets (أَسَاوِر, *asāwir*) of gold, and pearls﴾ (وَلُؤْلُؤًا, *wa lu'lu'an*), studded with gold (مُرَصَّع بِالذَّهَبِ, *muraṣṣa' bi'l-dhahab*).
﴿And they will say, "All praise is for Allah, who has removed from us grief﴾ entirely, ﴿Indeed, our Lord is Forgiving﴾ of sins, ﴿Appreciative﴾ of obedience."

Tafsir al-Jalalayn (Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti) on surah 35, verse 35:

﴿The One Who has caused us to dwell in the abode of permanence (al-muqamah), by His bounty. No fatigue (nasab) touches us therein, nor does weariness (lughub) touch us therein.﴾ Al-iqamah (permanence, lasting dwelling); nasab means toil or hardship; lughub means exhaustion resulting from toil, because there is no obligation (taklif) therein. He mentioned the second, which follows the first, to explicitly negate it.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 35, verse 36:

﴿And those who disbelieve, for them is the fire of Hell. It will not be decreed for them [to die] so that they would die﴾ [by death], ﴿and [thus] rest﴾, ﴿nor will its punishment be lightened for them﴾ even for the blink of an eye. ﴿Thus do We recompense every ungrateful one﴾ disbeliever. [The verb is read] with the ya' and with a nun that is fatha-vowelled, with kasra on the zay, and with a fatha on ﴿kulla﴾ (every).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 35, verse 37:

﴿And they will cry out therein﴾ (yastaghithun), crying out with intense distress and wailing, saying: ﴿"Our Lord, bring us out﴾ from it, ﴿so we may do righteousness, other than what we used to do"﴾. Then it will be said to them: ﴿"Did We not give you a life long enough﴾ (waqtan) ﴿for whoever would be mindful to be mindful therein? And there came to you the warner﴾ (al-rasul), but you did not respond. ﴿So taste [it], for the wrongdoers﴾ (al-kafirin) ﴿have no helper"﴾, one who would repel the punishment from them.

Indeed, Allah is the Knower of the unseen of the heavens and the earth; indeed He is the Knower of what is in the breasts (﴿بِذاتِ الصُّدُور﴾), that is, of what is in the hearts. So His knowledge of other than that is more fitting for consideration with regard to the state of the people.

He it is Who made you successors (khalā'if) on the earth. (Khalā'if is the plural of khalīfah, meaning that some of you succeed others.) ﴿Whoever disbelieves﴾ among you, ﴿upon him is his disbelief﴾, i.e., the burden (wabāl) of his disbelief. ﴿And their disbelief does not increase the disbelievers in their Lord's sight except in hatred﴾, i.e., anger. ﴿And their disbelief does not increase the disbelievers except in loss﴾ for the Hereafter.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 35, verse 40:

﴿Say: "Have you considered your associates whom you invoke﴾ worship ﴿besides Allah﴾, that is, other than Him, and they are the idols whom you claimed to be Allah's associates? ﴿Show me﴾ inform me ﴿what they have created of the earth, or do they have a partnership﴾ a shared role ﴿with Allah﴾ in the creation ﴿of the heavens? Or have We given them a Book so they are upon clear evidence﴾ a proof ﴿from it﴾ that they have a partnership with Me?" No, none of that. ﴿Rather, the wrongdoers﴾ the disbelievers ﴿promise one another﴾ nothing ﴿but delusion﴾ falsehood, by their saying that the idols will intercede for them.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 35, verse 41:

﴿Indeed, Allah holds the heavens and the earth lest they cease⦆ — that is, He prevents them from ceasing (zawal). ﴿And if they were to cease⦆ — the lam here is the lam of oath (lam al-qasam) — ﴿if they ceased, none could hold them⦆ — the ma here is negating (in) — ﴿from anyone after Him⦆ — that is, other than Him. ﴿Indeed, He is ever Forbearing, Forgiving⦆ — in delaying the punishment of the disbelievers.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 35, verse 42:

﴿And they swore by Allah with the utmost of their oaths﴾, i.e., the disbelievers of Makkah, ﴿with the utmost of their effort in them﴾, meaning their greatest exertion in swearing, ﴿that if a warner [i.e., a Messenger] came to them, they would be more guided than any one of the (previous) nations﴾, namely the Jews, the Christians and others, i.e., than any single one of them, because of what they saw of some of them denying others, when the Jews said: "The Christians are not upon anything," and the Christians said: "The Jews are not upon anything." ﴿But when a warner came to them﴾, i.e., Muhammad ﷺ, ﴿it only increased them in aversion﴾, i.e., in distance from guidance.

﴿اسْتِكْبارًا فِي الأَرْض﴾ ("arrogance in the land") عَنْ الإيمان. مَفْعُول لَهُ (object of purpose, an accusative noun giving the reason for the action). ﴿ومَكْر﴾ ("and scheming") العَمَل ﴿السَّيِّئ﴾ ("the evil deed") مِن الشِّرْك وغَيْره ("from polytheism and other things"). ﴿ولا يَحِيق﴾ ("and does not befall") يُحِيط ("encompass"). ﴿المَكْر السَّيِّئ إلّا بِأَهْلِهِ﴾ ("the evil scheming except to its own people") وهُوَ الماكِر ("and they are the schemers"). وَوَصْف المَكْر بِالسَّيْءِ أصْل ("describing the scheming as evil is the original usage"). وإضافَته إلَيْهِ قِيلَ: اسْتِعْمال آخَر ("and its attribution to it [the evil] is said to be another usage") قُدِّرَ فِيهِ مُضاف ("in which an omitted noun is assumed") حَذَرًا مِن الإضافَة إلى الصِّفَة ("to avoid attributing a noun to an adjective"). Here "إضافة" (idafa, construct phrase) is the grammatical term for a genitive construction linking two nouns.

﴿فَهَلْ يَنْظُرُونَ﴾ ("So do they await") يَنْتَظِرُونَ ﴿إلّا سُنَّة الأَوَّلِينَ﴾ ("except the way of the former peoples") سُنَّة اللَّه فِيهِمْ مِن تَعْذِيبهمْ بِتَكْذِيبِهِمْ رُسُلهمْ ("God's way with them, of punishing them for denying their messengers"). ﴿فَلَنْ تَجِد لِسُنَّةِ اللَّه تَبْدِيلًا ولَنْ تَجِد لِسُنَّةِ اللَّه تَحْوِيلًا﴾ ("So you will not find any change in God's way, and you will not find any diversion in God's way") أيْ لا يُبَدَّل بِالعَذابِ غَيْره ("that is, punishment is not exchanged for anything other than it") ولا يَحُول إلى غَيْر مُسْتَحِقّه ("and it is not diverted to anyone other than those who deserve it").

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 35, verse 44:

﴿Have they not travelled through the land and seen how was the end of those before them, though they were greater than them in strength?﴾ So Allah destroyed them for their denial of their messengers. ﴿And Allah is not to be frustrated by anything in the heavens or on the earth.﴾ That is, He is not outstripped or escaped by anything. ﴿Indeed, He is ever Knowing﴾ of all things, ﴿Competent﴾ over them.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 35, verse 45:

﴿And if Allah were to seize mankind for what they have earned﴾ of sins, ﴿He would not leave upon its back﴾ i.e., the earth ﴿any creature﴾ (nasama: a living soul) ﴿moving upon it﴾ ﴿but He defers them until a specified term﴾ i.e., the Day of Resurrection. ﴿And when their term comes, indeed Allah is ever Seeing of His servants﴾ so He will recompense them for their deeds, rewarding the believers and punishing the disbelievers.
